{{Duration|m=4|s=16}} (album version) | label = [[RSO Records|RSO]] | writer = [[Barry Gibb]], Andy Gibb | producer = [[Gibb-Galuten-Richardson]] | prev_title = [[I Just Want to Be Your Everything]] | prev_year = 1977 | next_title = [[Shadow Dancing (song)|Shadow Dancing]] | next_year = 1978 }} "'''(Love Is) Thicker Than Water'''" is a song performed by [[Andy Gibb]], released in September 1977 as the second and final single by [[RSO Records]] from his debut album, ''[[Flowing Rivers]]'' (1977). The song was his second single that topped the [[US Billboard Hot 100]]. It was mainly written by [[Barry Gibb]], with help from Andy Gibb and produced by [[Gibb-Galuten-Richardson]]. The B-side of this song was "[[Words and Music (song)|Words and Music]]" in the US, but "Flowing Rivers" in the UK.{{cite web|url=http://www.columbia.edu/~brennan/beegees/77.html |title=Gibb Songs: 1977 |last=Brennan |first=Joseph |access-date=14 June 2013}} It became a [[Music recording sales certification|gold record]]. ''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' magazine describes the song as "a midtempo ballad that changes pace from a lushly romantic and soft [Andy] Gibb vocal to an uptempo instrumental drive. Plenty of melody and another catchy hook".{{cite web|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=sEUEAAAAMBAJ&q=love+is+thicker+than+water+andy+gibb&pg=PT101 |title=Billboard Top Single Picks |date=5 November 1977 |publisher=[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |access-date=30 December 2014}} ''[[Cash Box]]'' said that "the choral harmonies are full of pop appeal, while the [[arrangement (music)|arrangement]] adds a grandiose touch that will attract more progressive tastes."{{cite news|title=CashBox Singles Reviews|date=November 5, 1977|page=22|newspaper=Cash Box|accessdate=2021-12-26|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Cash-Box/70s/1977/CB-1977-11-05.pdf}}

{{Duration|m=4|s=16}} (album version) | label = RSO | writer = Barry Gibb, Andy Gibb | producer = Gibb-Galuten-Richardson | prev_title = I Just Want to Be Your Everything | prev_year = 1977 | next_title = Shadow Dancing | next_year = 1978 }} "(Love Is) Thicker Than Water" is a song performed by Andy Gibb, released in September 1977 as the second and final single by RSO Records from his debut album, Flowing Rivers (1977). The song was his second single that topped the US Billboard Hot 100. It was mainly written by Barry Gibb, with help from Andy Gibb and produced by Gibb-Galuten-Richardson. The B-side of this song was "Words and Music" in the US, but "Flowing Rivers" in the UK. It became a gold record. Billboard magazine describes the song as "a midtempo ballad that changes pace from a lushly romantic and soft [Andy] Gibb vocal to an uptempo instrumental drive. Plenty of melody and another catchy hook". Cash Box said that "the choral harmonies are full of pop appeal, while the arrangement adds a grandiose touch that will attract more progressive tastes."

sections.heading: Writing and recording
sections.wikitext:
"(Love Is) Thicker Than Water" was written by [[Barry Gibb]] in [[Bermuda]] with Andy Gibb credited as co-writer.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://bernews.com/2013/03/island-ignited-bee-gees-musical-fever/ |title=Island Ignited Bee Gees' Musical "Fever" |publisher=Bernews |access-date=11 June 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141230133843/http://bernews.com/2013/03/island-ignited-bee-gees-musical-fever/ |archive-date=30 December 2014 |url-status = live}}</ref> Andy Gibb later revealed writing a song with Barry:

{{cquote|I did one song with Barry, 'Thicker Than Water' which I thought was good", Gibb explains, "Even though it says on the credits 'B. & A. Gibb', it is really Barry's song - it is very hard to write with Barry, but he said, 'Help me think of a great title'. That was a period where Barry was thinking of titles first and seeing how they would inspire him to write a song. I said, 'How about Thicker Than Water?' I did not say 'Love Is' just 'Thicker Than Water', he said 'That's great!' and then he came up with 'Love is higher than a mountain' and he just went on from there, but the title was totally my idea.<ref name="he">{{cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=KugbDQHX0R8C&q=love+is+thicker+than+water&pg=PT848 |title=The Bee Gees - Tales of the Brothers Gibb |last=Hughes |first=Andrew |year=2009 |isbn=9780857120045 |access-date=30 December 2014}}</ref>}}

"(Love Is) Thicker than Water" was recorded in October 1976 at the [[Criteria Studios]] in [[Miami]], [[Florida]], during the same time as "[[I Just Want to Be Your Everything]]".  On the two tracks, [[Joe Walsh]] of [[Eagles (band)|Eagles]] played guitar.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.columbia.edu/~brennan/beegees/76.html |title=Gibb Songs: 1976 |last=Brennan |first=Joseph |access-date=14 June 2013}}</ref> The song was certified Gold in the United States on 16 February 1978 as [[Robert Stigwood]]  presented Gibb with his first gold record at the Roxy in [[Los Angeles]].<ref name="he"/>

''[[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]]'' reviewed the song concluding that it has "plenty of melody and another catchy hook."<ref>{{cite news|title=Top Single Picks|newspaper=Billboard|access-date=2020-07-11|page=104|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-Billboard/70s/1977/Billboard%201977-11-05.pdf|date=November 5, 1977}}</ref> ''[[Record World]]'' said that it "flows with a light touch and a clever chorus/hook."<ref name=rw>{{cite magazine|magazine=Record World|date=November 5, 1977|accessdate=2023-02-16|title=Hits of the Week|page=1|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/Archive-All-Music/Record-World/70s/77/RW-1977-11-05.pdf}}</ref>
sections.text:
"(Love Is) Thicker Than Water" was written by Barry Gibb in Bermuda with Andy Gibb credited as co-writer. Andy Gibb later revealed writing a song with Barry:

{{cquote|I did one song with Barry, 'Thicker Than Water' which I thought was good", Gibb explains, "Even though it says on the credits 'B. & A. Gibb', it is really Barry's song - it is very hard to write with Barry, but he said, 'Help me think of a great title'. That was a period where Barry was thinking of titles first and seeing how they would inspire him to write a song. I said, 'How about Thicker Than Water?' I did not say 'Love Is' just 'Thicker Than Water', he said 'That's great!' and then he came up with 'Love is higher than a mountain' and he just went on from there, but the title was totally my idea.}}

"(Love Is) Thicker than Water" was recorded in October 1976 at the Criteria Studios in Miami, Florida, during the same time as "I Just Want to Be Your Everything".  On the two tracks, Joe Walsh of Eagles played guitar. The song was certified Gold in the United States on 16 February 1978 as Robert Stigwood  presented Gibb with his first gold record at the Roxy in Los Angeles.

Billboard reviewed the song concluding that it has "plenty of melody and another catchy hook." Record World said that it "flows with a light touch and a clever chorus/hook."

sections.heading: Aftermath
sections.wikitext:
As evidence of the Gibb brothers' U.S. chart domination in 1978, atop the March 4, 1978 Hot 100 the [[Bee Gees]]' "[[Stayin' Alive]]" was displaced by this song,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://allmusic.com/artist/andy-gibb-p13045/charts-awards/billboard-singles|title=Andy Gibb's ''Billboard'' singles history|publisher=[[Rovi Corporation]] / [[Billboard (magazine)|Billboard]] |access-date=2011-12-16}}</ref> which in turn was displaced two weeks later by the Bee Gees' "[[Night Fever]]", which in turn was displaced eight weeks later by [[Yvonne Elliman]]'s "[[If I Can't Have You (Bee Gees song)|If I Can't Have You]]".  Since [[Barry Gibb]] had a hand in writing all four of these songs, he became the only person in history to write four consecutive US number-one singles, a feat unmatched to this day.

The song was released in February 1978 in [[Netherlands]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.discogs.com/Andy-Gibb-Love-Is-Thicker-Than-Water/release/2766606 |title=Andy Gibb - (Love Is) Thicker than Water |date=February 1978 |publisher=[[Discogs]] |access-date=14 June 2013}}</ref>

On October 7, 1977 Andy performed the song, and "I Just Want to Be Your Everything", on ''[[The Midnight Special (TV series)|The Midnight Special]]''.
sections.text:
As evidence of the Gibb brothers' U.S. chart domination in 1978, atop the March 4, 1978 Hot 100 the Bee Gees' "Stayin' Alive" was displaced by this song, which in turn was displaced two weeks later by the Bee Gees' "Night Fever", which in turn was displaced eight weeks later by Yvonne Elliman's "If I Can't Have You".  Since Barry Gibb had a hand in writing all four of these songs, he became the only person in history to write four consecutive US number-one singles, a feat unmatched to this day.

The song was released in February 1978 in Netherlands.

On October 7, 1977 Andy performed the song, and "I Just Want to Be Your Everything", on The Midnight Special.
